properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a first /feedback report windows "since the ledger began" and never says when that was, or that the design is older. The ledger is a per-machine sidecar, born with v0.59.0 or with the store on a new machine. The design keeps no birth date, and the report prints the first call as raw unix seconds. Same shape as changelog_view's open window and since_export on a store with no export
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (the hxm_program hub's first /feedback report, 2026-09-14, reflow2 0.60.2) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "The ledger is younger than the design. 370 nodes, 51 ledger lines. It began with this version, so a project's first /feedback renders a window that can look like a quiet 86 minutes and misrepresent months of work. `window_described` does say 'since the ledger began', which is the right instinct; naming the ledger's own start date beside the design's size would make the gap unmissable." The report itself read "49 calls across 13 tools, 2026-09-14 09:40 → 11:06 (86 minutes)", for a hub written to since August and minted on 0.23.0.
EXPECTED: a reader of a first report can see that the window covers a sliver of the design's life.
NOT AFFECTED: later reports ("since the previous report") and reports with a named `since` date.
The same section's third point ("168 of 181 served tools never called", the report and reconcile families uncalled during a status-report session) is already root-caused in fact:root-cause-the-status-claim-was-keyed-to-nothing-and-the-catalogue-spoke-the-designs-side-not-the-askers and is not repeated here.

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the reporter's words): no record of the ledger's age as a defect. The nearest is fact:the-first-real-usage-report-classed-four-of-five-refusals-as-other, where reflow2's own design met the same limit on 2026-09-12 ("the ledger has no baseline before today") and recorded it as a note.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) REPORT SHAPE (contract): usage_report states the window's start in words. It carries neither the ledger's birth as a labelled date nor anything about the design before it.
(B) SUBSTRATE: the design keeps no birth date, so "older than the ledger" cannot be computed as a date comparison.
(C) THE LEDGER IS PER MACHINE: a sidecar beside the store, never exported, so it restarts on every new machine or import. Its start is not a property of the design.
(D) INSTRUCTION: the feedback skill never tells the agent that a first report may cover a fraction of the design's life.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: 0.74.0 (or 0.60.2) already names the ledger's start.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM:
· E predicts a labelled ledger-start field in the reply.
· A predicts only `window: {"from": "beginning_of_ledger"}` and an unlabelled first_call_unix.
· B predicts no date in the design's identity.
· C predicts a different ledger start on a second checkout of the same design.
· D predicts no such sentence in the skill.

⑤ RESULTS:
· 0.74.0 on a scratch store (usage_report, peek): the reply carries four things. `window_described: "since the ledger began (no previous report)"`. `tally.window: {"from": "beginning_of_ledger"}`, with no date. `tally.first_call_unix`, the first line's time in raw unix seconds, not labelled as the ledger's birth. `environment.design_nodes`, the size now. Nothing relates them. In code, usage.rs WindowStart::BeginningOfLedger carries no timestamp, and skills_tools.rs usage_report adds no ledger-start or design-age field. ⇒ A HOLDS. E is QUALIFIED: the date is on the page (the reporter rendered it as 09:40 → 11:06), but only as the first call's time, never as "the ledger began here, and the design is older".
· Design identity (identity.rs, `.id.json`) holds graph_id, label, origin and minted_by, and no date. minted_by is machine-local: the hxm_program checkout on the maintainer's machine reads `origin: adopted, minted_by: 0.66.0` (2026-09-23) for a design first minted on 0.23.0. ⇒ B HOLDS. The server cannot say how old the design is. It can say how big the design is and when the ledger began.
· That second-machine checkout of the same hxm design has its own ledger: 44 calls, first 2026-09-23 10:44, all from `reflow2-mcp --call 0.66.0` (the import session), against a committed export of 493 nodes. reflow2's own ledger begins 2026-09-12 14:52, when #490's binary went live. ⇒ C HOLDS: a ledger starts at whichever came last, v0.59.0 reaching the project or the store being created on that machine.
· getting-started/skills/feedback/SKILL.md, step 1, says the window is "since the previous report", and its limits say the window is the project's, not the session's. There is no sentence about a first report or a ledger younger than the design. ⇒ D HOLDS.

⑥ CLASS: a windowed report states where its window begins, never how much of its subject lies before it. The design keeps no clock by choice (dec:loop-status-state-not-history). So each windowed read borrows a baseline from somewhere else: a sidecar, a release, a committed export. When that baseline is younger than the design, or absent, the report presents a short or empty window as a quiet one. Two other members are already recorded, and were not re-measured here:
· changelog_view with no deployed release. Its note says the window "is open from the beginning of the design" while it returns 0 entries from 41 dated events (hxm 2026-09-14, item F-25; fact:changelog-view-is-step-two-of-the-cut-and-returns-nothing-for-a-real-cut).
· loop_status since_export on a store with no committed export ("EVERY node counts as new", in fact:root-cause-no-served-read-answers-since-last-time-2026-09-28).
A fix to usage_report alone would not have stopped the changelog_view report.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE; no code was changed. A test pinning the class would assert this: every windowed read whose baseline starts after the design's first content, or that has no baseline, says so in a field. It gives its baseline's start as a date and what the design already held then.
· usage_report: `ledger_began`, and the design's node count when the ledger began.
· changelog_view and since_export: that no baseline exists, and what that means for the window.

PROPOSED FIX, the reporter's own, recorded here rather than as a new idea because it is the direct answer to (A) and (D):
· name the ledger's start date beside the design's size in the report;
· have the feedback skill say plainly, on a first report, that the window covers the ledger's life, not the design's.
One cheap addition makes the comparison computable despite (B): write the design's node count on the ledger's first line, or on every report marker.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS:
· HELD: the ledger is younger than the design, and naming its start beside the design's size would make the gap visible.
· QUALIFIED: "it began with this version" is one of two ways a ledger starts. The other is a new machine or an import, measured on the same design. The start date is in the reply today as first_call_unix, unlabelled.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
· whether a reader shown a labelled "ledger began" line reads the window correctly (untested);
· what the hxm work machine's ledger holds (not read);
· whether a ledger should travel with the design, committed or exported. That was not examined, and it would meet req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content.
